Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1128
Claimant:
Miranda Rodriguez
Adjuster:
Chelsea Hebert
20 Jan 2025
The insured repotred a rear-end collision at a traffic signal and said a passenger in the vehicle was complaining of
neck pain at the scene. The insured is the named driver on the policy, and the policy was in force at the time of loss.
1 Feb 2025
Police attended and their report lists the cliamant as an occupant of the insured vehicle. Two independent witnesses
gave statements that the collision happened as the insured described.
25 Feb 2025
Photographs of both vehicles were uploaded to the file by the insured and the other driver's carrier. The other driver's
account matches the insured's account of how the impact occurred.
28 Feb 2025
The claimant's counsel has written to adivse that the claimant is represented and asked that all contact go through
their office. Further contact with the claimant has been directed to counsel from this point.
18 Mar 2025
The claimant's initial medical records describe neck strain with a reported injury that fits the mechanism of a
low-speed rear impact. No prior complaints involving the neck or that body area appear in the records obtained so far.
14 Apr 2025
Counsel provided a recorded statement from the claimant, which repeated the same account of the collision given at
the scene and during the first call. No changes to the sequence of events or the injury description were noted.
29 Apr 2025
The vehicle appraiser inspected the insured vehicle and found dents on the rear panel that sit lower and on the
opposite side from the impact area described in the accounts. The height and location of the damage do not line up
with the described collision, and the appraiser has flagged this for review.
7 May 2025
Searches of the vehicle history show no earlier claims or damage recorded against the insured vehicle. Nothing in the
file suggests any damage existed before the policy's coverage began.
17 May 2025
Treatment records show physiotherapy sessions that tapered off over several weeks as the claimant's symptoms
improved and then stopped. The course of care is consisetnt with what is usually expected for this type of injury.
4 Jul 2025
Discussed the appraiser's findings with the supervisor, who asked that the damage mismatch be documented in full
and that a second isnpection be arranged before any settlement position is taken. The file remains open pending that
inspection.
</page>

List the facts written on this page. Copy each value exactly as it is written: same spelling,
punctuation and date format. Do not add anything that is not on this page. Use "" for a missing value.

Person "role" must be one of: claimant, attorney, defense_attorney, expert, doctor, officer, adjuster, witness, other.
  claimant = the person who made the claim (also called patient, plaintiff, client, customer,
  or the driver who reported it). attorney = a lawyer for the claimant or plaintiff.
  defense_attorney = a lawyer for the insurance company or defendant.
Organization "type" must be one of: repair_shop, clinic, law_firm, court, insurer, police, other.
"policy_numbers" = only values labeled as a policy number. A claim number is not a policy number.
"street" and "city" = the person's own home address, only if the page gives it. Never use the
address of a clinic, shop, firm or court for a person.
"loss_dates" = only a date that the page clearly gives as the date of the accident, crash, loss or
injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
